$comment: Relic id -> name tables for relics[] / gemstones[] in export-schema.json. Static game metadata, not account data. Read live off game build 11.67.0 (RslCompanionExtraction, `BlessingProbe --relics` and `--l10n`). Deliberately SMALL: the only opaque id in the relic payload that this file can honestly name is the socket shape. Relic and gemstone typeId are a catalog of the game - name, rarity, group, skill, stat bonuses - and belong in a champion-index-style catalog keyed on typeId, not in a name table here. Each table below states how it was derived AND how strong that derivation is.

socketShapes.$comment: relics[].sockets[].shapeKindId, from the game's IL2CPP `RelicStoneShapeKindId` enum. A gemstone only fits a socket of its own shape, so this is the field that decides what can be socketed where.
socketShapes.source: IL2CPP enum RelicStoneShapeKindId (member list), plus the observed value set across 645 live sockets
socketShapes.confidence: PARTIAL - ids are certain, labels are inferred. READ THIS BEFORE USING THE NAMES.
provenance: The enum declares exactly five members, in this order: Circle, Triangle, Square, Diamond, Pentagon.

The live data carries exactly five distinct values, 1-5, across 645 sockets on 377 relics (1x313, 2x92, 3x67, 4x91, 5x82). Five members and five contiguous values from 1 means the mapping is a bijection onto 1..5.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: which member is 1. The binding below assumes declaration order starting at 1, and nothing independent confirms it. IL2CPP enum members can carry explicit values - ArtifactSetKindId's do, which is exactly how the artifact set table came to be wrong from id 4 onward before 2026-08-02 - and ListFields reports member names without their values.

An independent check is available to anyone with the game open: 313 of 645 sockets are shapeKindId 1, so if the most common socket shape on screen is not a circle, this table is wrong. It has not been performed.
Consumers: treat shapeKindId as the authoritative value and these names as provisional labels. Join on the id. Do not persist the label as if it were data from the game.

upgradeCurrencies.$comment: The resource ids that upgrade a relic. They appear in resources[] like any other resource; listed here because the relationship between them and relics[].rank / relics[].level is the part a consumer cannot see from the payload alone.
upgradeCurrencies.source: live resources/items dicts, cross-checked against the in-game balances and against the game's own description strings
upgradeCurrencies.confidence: HIGH - ids matched live balances exactly and the names are the game's own strings
provenance: The five Basalt ids sit in the ITEMS dict and matched the in-game balances 10/17/10/5/1 in rank order on 2026-08-03 - five values in sequence, so not a coincidence of one number.
Starstone sits in the RESOURCES dict and matched 19466.

Names are quoted from the game's own strings, not from a wiki: 'Rank 1 Basalt. Used to upgrade a Rank 1 Relic to Rank 2.' and 'You'll need to use a new resource - Starstones - to level up your Relics.'
All six were absent from the extraction engine's exclusive resource allowlist and were therefore DROPPED from every export before schema 11, however many the account held.

values.name: Starstone
values.note: Levels a relic up. relics[].level steps by 3 (0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 observed).

values.name: Rank 1 Basalt
values.note: Raises a Rank 1 relic to Rank 2.

values.name: Rank 2 Basalt
values.note: Raises a Rank 2 relic to Rank 3.

values.name: Rank 3 Basalt
values.note: Raises a Rank 3 relic to Rank 4.

values.name: Rank 4 Basalt
values.note: Raises a Rank 4 relic to Rank 5.

values.name: Rank 5 Basalt
values.note: Raises a Rank 5 relic to Rank 6. No rank-6 relic was present on the reference account, but the currency for reaching one exists.

relicTypes.$comment: relics[].typeId -> relic name. The wire carries only the id; join here.
relicTypes.source: l10n:relic/name?id=N#static, read live from process memory (RslCompanionExtraction BlessingProbe --l10n "l10n:relic/")
relicTypes.confidence: HIGH for the 88 ids captured - real localized strings, not placeholders. INCOMPLETE: the relic-icon atlas (RSL-game-assets, 2026-09-07) shows typeIds through 94 now exist; 89-94 postdate this capture and are unnamed.
provenance: An earlier read returned SharedLTextKey.DefaultValue placeholders ("Relic 12 name") for every id, and this file used to state relic names could not be resolved. That was a lazy-load artefact, not a game fact: l10n:relic strings hydrate only once the in-game Relic screen has been opened. With it open on 2026-08-03 all 88 resolved to real names (1 Unholy Grail, 16 Aspect of Siroth, 88 The Towerhelm).
Sibling-offset scoring: offsets +8, +32 and -16 each returned 88 distinct names; +8 was used. 528 l10n:relic strings across name/description/lore.
ids 1-88 are contiguous with no gaps.
Re-capture: dotnet run --project extraction/tools/BlessingProbe -- --l10n "l10n:relic/" --cache extraction/offsets_cache.json (game running, Relic screen opened once).

gemstoneTypes.$comment: gemstones[].typeId -> gemstone name. The UI calls them gemstones; the game class is RelicStone.
gemstoneTypes.source: l10n:relic-stone/name?id=N#static, read live from process memory (BlessingProbe --l10n "l10n:relic-stone/")
gemstoneTypes.confidence: HIGH for ids 1-119. id 120 omitted: its name and description keys are transposed in the 2026-08-03 capture (name key -> the ATK-stacking description text, description key -> "Lifedrain"), so it is withheld pending a clean re-capture rather than shipped wrong.
provenance: 120 name strings and 120 description strings resolved on 2026-08-03 (e.g. 1 Shieldbreaker, 17 Unstoppable, 20 Quickstrike). ids 1-119 are contiguous and each reads as a name.

For id 120, description="Lifedrain" (reads as a name) and name=the ATK-stacking bonus text (reads as a description) - swapped for that one entry. Its real name is most likely Lifedrain, not shipped as fact here.
Previously withheld from this file as catalog data. It lands here on the same reasoning heroes[].blessingId gets blessing_index.json: nothing else ships a relic/gemstone catalog yet.

notNamedHere.$comment: Ids the payload carries that this file still does NOT name, and why.
notNamedHere.relicTypeId_89_to_94: relicTypes above names ids 1-88. The relic-icon atlas (RSL-game-assets) shows typeIds through 94 exist as of build 11.75.0; 89-94 postdate the 2026-08-03 l10n capture and need a re-run with the Relic screen open.
notNamedHere.gemstoneTypeId_120: gemstoneTypes above names ids 1-119. id 120's name/description keys are transposed in the capture - see the provenance note there.
notNamedHere.relicRarity: Not on the account record at all. RelicType.Rarity and RelicStoneType.Rarity are catalog fields reached through a shared type object, which the client hydrates lazily - the same trap that silently zeroed heroes[].factionId for 340 of 957 champions. Reading them per record would produce holes that look like data. relicTypes / gemstoneTypes name the id only; no rarity, group or bonus text.
